OpenAI’s market share is slipping.


Kenshi (@kenshii_ai)

ChatGPT is dying.

OpenAI lost the crown as their market share fell below 40 percent for the first time ever.

It stands at just 38.7 percent now after four straight months of brutal decline.

Six months ago it still ruled with 52 percent but the hype is collapsing fast.

The monopoly is finished and users are finally turning to real competition that actually delivers.

The era of OpenAI supremacy is over for good

Amazon’s AI coding boom is creating a mess. 

Vibe coding their way to chaos.


Hedgie (@HedgieMarkets)

🦔The internal document was reported by Business Insider. Here’s the link: businessinsider.com/ai-spraw…




— https://nitter.net/HedgieMarkets/status/2046092412380950765#m

“AI is at best a functional mimic, not a conscious experiencing subject. …. The real moral issue lies not in making AI conscious …. but in avoiding transforming humans into zombies”


Anna Ciaunica PhD @annaciaunica.bsky.social (@AnnaCiaunica)

Hi @GaryMarcus ! We have a paper arguing exactly this - would love your thoughts on it 🙏

arxiv.org/abs/2601.21016




— https://nitter.net/AnnaCiaunica/status/2046133366886469719#m
Claude’s “emotion” vectors are “emotionlike” in roughly the same sense that counterfeit “money” is “moneylike”.

Importantly, the tweet by @itsolelehmann may be misleading. I stand by what I said but have some reason to think that @AmandaAskell’s views may have been misrepresented.

Seeking clarification and will update when I have more info.

OMG.  Let’s get one thing straight. Claude doesn’t get anxious. 

It mimics people who get anxious.

Those two things are NOT the same.

My head is shaking so much I need medical attention.


Ole Lehmann (@itsolelehmann)

anthropic's in-house philosopher thinks claude gets anxious.

and when you trigger its anxiety, your outputs get worse.

her name is amanda askell.

she specializes in claude's psychology (how the model behaves, how it thinks about its own situation, what values it holds)

good to know that a trillion dollars’ investment scaling has thoroughly solved the challenges of common sense.


OPT (@optelca)







— https://nitter.net/optelca/status/2045654285061599670#m

Is a 92% “honest”* AI really good enough?

Or a disaster waiting to happen?

—-
*”honest” is itself a misleading anthropomorphization of the kind Anthropic loves to promote.  “Accurate” would be more accurate.

Dario is not as different from Sam as people seem to think.


Austen Allred (@Austen)

Honest question:

Why does he keep saying this?



— https://nitter.net/Austen/status/2045324619318444322#m
The only way SpaceX’s anticipated IPO price makes sense?

“my honest read is that a significant portion of this spending is driven by competitive fear rather than demonstrated returns. Nobody wants to be the company that didn't invest in AI when everyone else did. That's how bubbles get funded, and at some point boards are going to demand a number that justifies it.”


Hedgie (@HedgieMarkets)

🦔Goldman Sachs reports that companies are blowing past their AI inference budgets by orders of magnitude, with inference costs in engineering now approaching 10%

Everyone’s quitting but everything’s going great. AGI will be here next week. Scout’s honor!


Max Zeff (@ZeffMax)

This story has now been updated with more details. Three leaders departed from OpenAI today:

- Kevin Weil, VP of OpenAI for Science
- Srinivas Narayanan, CTO of B2B Applications
- Bill Peebles, Head of Sora



— https://nitter.net/ZeffMax/status/2045248266384838800#m

“The sharpest drop came from people who used the model for direct answers, not from those who used it more like a hint system, which suggests the real issue is not AI exposure itself but replacing effort with completion.

The result is not that AI makes people less capable by default, but that answer outsourcing can shrink the mental effort that normally trains skill.”

Even more results on the dangers of outsourcing your thinking to AI.


Rohan Paul (@rohanpaul_ai)

BIG claim from new MIT + Oxf

Can people please stop taking shots at @sama, and boycott his company instead?

Violence is not the answer.


Yuchen Jin (@Yuchenj_UW)

This is really bad.

The scary part in the US is that it doesn’t matter whether you are the CEO of OpenAI or just a regular PhD. There are paid online websites that can find your address and phone number.

I don’t know how such personal info got out.





— https://nitter.net/Yuchenj_UW/status/2043474166071128202#m
